I am 32, and I have worked this land my whole life — my mother taught me when I was small, and now it is my hands in the soil. Me and my husband have 4.1 mu of flat good land here in Quzhou. He goes out to construction work when jobs come, so we have a little cash, but every yuan I spend on the field is money we earned sweating. I watch what my neighbors do. If Auntie Li buys a certain seed and her wheat stands tall, I buy the same one. I don't trust new ideas unless I saw them work in the field next door.

For the wheat, I plough deep in October before sowing. I buy the improved wheat seed from the village shop — the same kind most people around here plant. I need about four bags of seed, which is about 25 jin per mu. Before I sow, I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer — the kind with numbers on it that the dealer sells — that is 80 jin for the whole field, about 20 jin per mu. Then in the spring, when the wheat wakes up, I spread urea. I use three and a half bags of urea for the wheat in total: one bag at green-up, one and a half bags at jointing when it shoots up fast, and one more half-bag at heading if the plants look a little yellow. That is about 170 jin of urea for 4 mu. I know it is a lot, but two years ago I tried to save money and used less, and the heads were small. Losing yield is a disaster; wasting a few jin of fertilizer is just a cost I can bear. I irrigate three times with our well: once before winter freeze so the wheat stores water, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray for weeds once in early spring, and if I see bugs on the leaves, I spray once more. Last year my wheat gave about 960 jin per mu. This year I hope for 1,000 jin, so I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat is cut in June, I plant hybrid maize seed straight into the wheat stubble without ploughing. The machine just drills it in. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer at planting time — same amount as wheat, about 20 jin per mu. Then at big-ear stage, when the cobs are forming, I spread two bags of urea. That timing is important — if you miss it, the cobs stay small. I irrigate twice: once after planting if the soil is dry, and once at big-ear stage. I spray for weeds once right after planting, and once for corn borer when I see moths flying in the evening. I expect about 1,120 jin per mu, which is about 560 kg per mu.

I do not buy separate potassium fertilizer. The compound fertilizer has some in it, and that has always been enough for my land. The dealer tried to sell me extra last year, but my cousin used it and saw no difference, so I keep my money.
